name: Insufficient Funds — Faster Payment Initiation (Exception Path EX-003)
description: PER-001 attempts to initiate a Faster Payment for an amount exceeding their available balance. The failure is detected synchronously at PaymentIntent creation time (POST /payments) by SVC-001 — no events are published. The channel receives a 402 error response and immediately shows the customer a specific, informative message with their available balance. No screening or fraud checks are triggered.

steps.action: Enter payment details: payee sort code + account number + name, amount £500.00
steps.note: Account available balance is £120.50 — insufficient for £500.00

steps.action: Display CoP match result. Prompt SCA.
POST /payments { account_id, amount: 500.00, payee details, cop_result: match, sca_assertion_ref }
Validate: account active ✓. Check available balance: £120.50 < £500.00. FAIL — insufficient funds. No PaymentIntent created. No events published.
Log rejected payment attempt (account_id, amount, failure_reason: insufficient_funds, timestamp)
steps.note: Logged without creating a PaymentIntent entity — no entity record for a rejected payment

steps.action: 402 Payment Required { error_code: INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, message: 'Available balance is insufficient for this payment', available_balance: '120.50' }
Display: 'Insufficient funds. Your available balance is £120.50. The payment has not been processed. Please reduce the amount or top up your account.'

outcome: Payment rejected at initiation. No PaymentIntent created. No events published. No screening or fraud checks triggered. Customer shown specific, informative error with their balance. FCA Consumer Duty outcome: customer understands why payment failed.
design_notes: Insufficient funds is detected synchronously at POST /payments — no async check required
No PaymentIntent entity is created for a failed initiation — this avoids polluting the PaymentIntent ledger with non-intents
The rejection is logged to SVC-103 for operational monitoring (failed payment attempt rate) but is not written to the WORM pipeline (not a regulatory audit event — no financial transaction occurred)
The customer can immediately retry with a lower amount or navigate to top-up flow
